member.name: M:VisioForge.Libs.ZXing.QrCode.Internal.FinderPatternFinder.handlePossibleCenter(System.Int32[],System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary:
This is called when a horizontal scan finds a possible alignment pattern. It will cross check with a vertical scan, and if successful, will, ah, cross-cross-check with another horizontal scan. This is needed primarily to locate the real horizontal center of the pattern in cases of extreme skew.
If that succeeds the finder pattern location is added to a list that tracks the number of times each location has been nearly-matched as a finder pattern. Each additional find is more evidence that the location is in fact a finder pattern center
member.param: reading state module counts from horizontal scan
row where finder pattern may be found
end of possible finder pattern in row
member.returns: true if a finder pattern candidate was found this time

member.name: M:CUDA.cuFFT.API.cufftGetSize(System.Int32,System.Int64@)
member.summary: Once plan generation has been done, either with the original API or the extensible API, this call returns the actual size of the work area required to support the plan. Callers who choose to manage work area allocation within their application must use this call after plan generation, and after any cufftSet*() calls subsequent to plan generation, if those calls might alter the required work space size.

member.name: M:CUDA.cuFFT.API.cufftSetWorkArea(System.Int32,System.IntPtr)
member.summary: cufftSetWorkArea() overrides the work area pointer associated with a plan. If the work area was auto-allocated, cuFFT frees the auto-allocated space. The cufftExecute*() calls assume that the work area pointer is valid and that it points to a contiguous region in device memory that does not overlap with any other work area. If this is not the case, results are indeterminate.

member.name: M:CUDA.cuFFT.API.cufftSetAutoAllocation(System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: cufftSetAutoAllocation() indicates that the caller intends to allocate and manage work areas for plans that have been generated. cuFFT default behavior is to allocate the work area at plan generation time. If cufftSetAutoAllocation() has been called with autoAllocate set to 0 ("false") prior to one of the cufftMakePlan*() calls, cuFFT does not allocate the work area. This is the preferred sequence for callers wishing to manage work area allocation.

member.name: M:CUDA.cuFFT.API.cufftXtSetWorkAreaPolicy(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.IntPtr)
member.summary: cufftXtSetWorkAreaPolicy() indicates that the caller intends to change work area size for a given plan handle.

member.summary: cufftExecC2C() (cufftExecZ2Z()) executes a single-precision (double-precision) complex-to-complex transform plan in the transform direction as specified by direction parameter. cuFFT uses the GPU memory pointed to by the idata parameter as input data. member.name: M:CUDA.cuFFT.GetSize(System.Int32)
member.summary: Once plan generation has been done, either with the original API or the extensible API, this call returns the actual size of the work area required to support the plan. Callers who choose to manage work area allocation within their application must use this call after plan generation, and after any cufftSet*() calls subsequent to plan generation, if those calls might alter the required work space size.

member.name: M:CUDA.cuFFT.SetWorkArea(System.Int32,System.IntPtr)
member.summary: cufftSetWorkArea() overrides the work area pointer associated with a plan. If the work area was auto-allocated, cuFFT frees the auto-allocated space. The cufftExecute*() calls assume that the work area pointer is valid and that it points to a contiguous region in device memory that does not overlap with any other work area. If this is not the case, results are indeterminate.

member.name: M:CUDA.cuFFT.SetAutoAllocation(System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: cufftSetAutoAllocation() indicates that the caller intends to allocate and manage work areas for plans that have been generated. cuFFT default behavior is to allocate the work area at plan generation time. If cufftSetAutoAllocation() has been called with autoAllocate set to 0 ("false") prior to one of the cufftMakePlan*() calls, cuFFT does not allocate the work area. This is the preferred sequence for callers wishing to manage work area allocation.

member.name: M:CUDA.cuFFT.ExecC2C(System.Int32,System.IntPtr,System.IntPtr,CUDA.cufftDirection)
member.summary: cufftExecC2C() (cufftExecZ2Z()) executes a single-precision (double-precision) complex-to-complex transform plan in the transform direction as specified by direction parameter. cuFFT uses the GPU memory pointed to by the idata parameter as input data. This function stores the Fourier coefficients in the odata array. If idata and odata are the same, this method does an in-place transform.

member.summary: cufftExecR2C() (cufftExecD2Z()) executes a single-precision (double-precision) real-to-complex, implicitly forward, cuFFT transform plan. cuFFT uses as input data the GPU memory pointed to by the idata parameter.

member.summary: (cuFFT) cufftXtCopyType_t is an enumerated type for multiple GPU functions that specifies the type of copy for cufftXtMemcpy().

member.name: F:CUDA.cufftXtCopyType.CUFFT_COPY_HOST_TO_DEVICE
member.summary: copies data from a contiguous host buffer to multiple device buffers, in the layout cuFFT requires for input data. dstPointer must point to a cudaLibXtDesc structure, and srcPointer must point to a host memory buffer.

member.name: F:CUDA.cufftXtCopyType.CUFFT_COPY_DEVICE_TO_HOST
member.summary: copies data from multiple device buffers, in the layout cuFFT produces for output data, to a contiguous host buffer. dstPointer must point to a host memory buffer, and srcPointer must point to a cudaLibXtDesc structure.

member.name: F:CUDA.cufftXtCopyType.CUFFT_COPY_DEVICE_TO_DEVICE
member.summary: copies data from multiple device buffers, in the layout cuFFT produces for output data, to multiple device buffers, in the layout cuFFT requires for input data. dstPointer and srcPointer must point to different cudaLibXtDesc structures (and therefore memory locations). That is, the copy cannot be in-place.

member.name: F:CUDA.Defines.CU_MEMHOSTALLOC_PORTABLE
member.summary: (Driver API) If set, host memory is portable between CUDA contexts. Flag for ::cuMemHostAlloc()

member.name: F:CUDA.Defines.CU_MEMHOSTALLOC_DEVICEMAP
member.summary: (Driver API) If set, host memory is mapped into CUDA address space and ::cuMemHostGetDevicePointer() may be called on the host pointer. Flag for ::cuMemHostAlloc()

member.name: F:CUDA.Defines.CU_MEMHOSTALLOC_WRITECOMBINED
member.summary: (Driver API) If set, host memory is portable between CUDA contexts. Flag for ::cuMemHostRegister()

member.name: F:CUDA.Defines.CU_MEMHOSTREGISTER_PORTABLE
member.summary: (Driver API) If set, host memory is portable between CUDA contexts. Flag for ::cuMemHostRegister()

member.name: F:CUDA.Defines.CU_MEMHOSTREGISTER_DEVICEMAP
member.summary: (Driver API) If set, host memory is mapped into CUDA address space and ::cuMemHostGetDevicePointer() may be called on the host pointer. Flag for ::cuMemHostRegister()

member.name: F:CUDA.Defines.CU_MEMHOSTREGISTER_IOMEMORY
member.summary:
(Driver API) If set, the passed memory pointer is treated as pointing to some memory-mapped I/O space, e.g.belonging to a third-party PCIe device.
On Windows the flag is a no-op.
On Linux that memory is marked as non cache-coherent for the GPU and is expected to be physically contiguous.It may return CUDA_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED if run as an unprivileged user, CUDA_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED on older Linux kernel versions. On all other platforms, it is not supported and CUDA_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED is returned. Flag for ::cuMemHostRegister()

member.name: F:CUDA.Defines.CUDA_ARRAY3D_LAYERED
member.summary: (Driver API) If set, the CUDA array is a collection of layers, where each layer is either a 1D or a 2D array and the Depth member of CUDA_ARRAY3D_DESCRIPTOR specifies the number of layers, not the depth of a 3D array.

member.name: F:CUDA.Defines.CUDA_ARRAY3D_2DARRAY
member.summary: (Driver API) Deprecated, use CUDA_ARRAY3D_LAYERED

member.name: F:CUDA.Defines.CUDA_ARRAY3D_COLOR_ATTACHMENT
member.summary: (Driver API) This flag indicates that the CUDA array may be bound as a color target in an external graphics API

member.name: F:CUDA.Defines.CUDA_ARRAY3D_SURFACE_LDST
member.summary: (Driver API) This flag must be set in order to bind a surface reference to the CUDA array

member.name: F:CUDA.Defines.CUDA_ARRAY3D_CUBEMAP
member.summary: (Driver API) If set, the CUDA array is a collection of six 2D arrays, representing faces of a cube.The width of such a CUDA array must be equal to its height, and Depth must be six. If ::CUDA_ARRAY3D_LAYERED flag is also set, then the CUDA array is a collection of cubemaps and Depth must be a multiple of six.

member.name: F:CUDA.Defines.CUDA_ARRAY3D_TEXTURE_GATHER
member.summary: (Driver API) This flag must be set in order to perform texture gather operations on a CUDA array.

member.name: F:CUDA.Defines.CUDA_ARRAY3D_DEPTH_TEXTURE
member.summary: (Driver API) This flag if set indicates that the CUDA array is a DEPTH_TEXTURE.

member.name: F:CUDA.Defines.CU_TRSA_OVERRIDE_FORMAT
member.summary: (Driver API) Override the texref format with a format inferred from the array. Flag for ::cuTexRefSetArray()

member.name: F:CUDA.Defines.CU_TRSF_READ_AS_INTEGER
member.summary: (Driver API) Read the texture as integers rather than promoting the values to floats in the range[0, 1]. Flag for ::cuTexRefSetFlags()

member.name: F:CUDA.Defines.CU_TRSF_NORMALIZED_COORDINATES
member.summary: (Driver API) Use normalized texture coordinates in the range[0, 1) instead of[0, dim). Flag for ::cuTexRefSetFlags()

member.name: F:CUDA.Defines.CU_TRSF_SRGB
member.summary: (Driver API) Perform sRGB->linear conversion during texture read. Flag for ::cuTexRefSetFlags()

member.name: F:CUDA.Defines.CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_END
member.summary: (Driver API) End of array terminator for the \p extra parameter to ::cuLaunchKernel

member.name: F:CUDA.Defines.CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_BUFFER_POINTER
member.summary: (Driver API) Indicator that the next value in the \p extra parameter to ::cuLaunchKernel will be a pointer to a buffer containing all kernel parameters used for launching kernel \p f.This buffer needs to honor all alignment/padding requirements of the individual parameters. If::CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_BUFFER_SIZE is not also specified in the \p extra array, then::CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_BUFFER_POINTER will have no effect.

member.name: F:CUDA.Defines.CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_BUFFER_SIZE
member.summary: (Driver API) Indicator that the next value in the \p extra parameter to ::cuLaunchKernel will be a pointer to a size_t which contains the size of the buffer specified with::CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_BUFFER_POINTER. It is required that ::CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_BUFFER_POINTER also be specified in the \p extra array if the value associated with ::CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_BUFFER_SIZE is not zero.

member.name: F:CUDA.Defines.CU_PARAM_TR_DEFAULT
member.summary: (Driver API) For texture references loaded into the module, use default texunit from texture reference.

member.name: T:CUDA.cublasStatus
member.summary: (cuBLAS) The type is used for function status returns. All cuBLAS library functions return their status.

member.name: F:CUDA.cublasStatus.CUBLAS_STATUS_SUCCESS
member.summary: The operation completed successfully.

member.name: F:CUDA.cublasStatus.CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_INITIALIZED
member.summary: The cuBLAS library was not initialized.

member.name: F:CUDA.cublasStatus.CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED
member.summary: Resource allocation failed inside the cuBLAS library.

member.name: F:CUDA.cublasStatus.CUBLAS_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE
member.summary: An unsupported value or parameter was passed to the function (a negative vector size, for example).

member.name: F:CUDA.cublasStatus.CUBLAS_STATUS_ARCH_MISMATCH
member.summary: The function requires a feature absent from the device architecture; usually caused by the lack of support for double precision.

member.name: F:CUDA.cublasStatus.CUBLAS_STATUS_MAPPING_ERROR
member.summary: An access to GPU memory space failed, which is usually caused by a failure to bind a texture.

member.name: F:CUDA.cublasStatus.CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED
member.summary: The GPU program failed to execute. This is often caused by a launch failure of the kernel on the GPU, which can be caused by multiple reasons.

member.name: F:CUDA.cublasStatus.CUBLAS_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR
member.summary: An internal cuBLAS operation failed. This error is usually caused by a cudaMemcpyAsync() failure.

member.name: F:CUDA.cublasStatus.CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED
member.summary: The functionnality requested is not supported

member.name: F:CUDA.cublasStatus.CUBLAS_STATUS_LICENSE_ERROR
member.summary: The functionnality requested requires some license and an error was detected when trying to check the current licensing.

member.name: T:CUDA.cublasOperation
member.summary: (cuBLAS) The cublasOperation_t type indicates which operation needs to be performed with the dense matrix. Its values correspond to Fortran characters ‘N’ or ‘n’ (non-transpose), ‘T’ or ‘t’ (transpose) and ‘C’ or ‘c’ (conjugate transpose) that are often used as parameters to legacy BLAS implementations.

member.name: F:CUDA.cublasOperation.CUBLAS_OP_N
member.summary: the non-transpose operation is selected

member.name: F:CUDA.cublasOperation.CUBLAS_OP_T
member.summary: the transpose operation is selected

member.name: F:CUDA.cublasOperation.CUBLAS_OP_C
member.summary: the conjugate transpose operation is selected

member.name: T:CUDA.cublasFillMode
member.summary: (cuBLAS) The type indicates which part (lower or upper) of the dense matrix was filled and consequently should be used by the function. Its values correspond to Fortran characters ‘L’ or ‘l’ (lower) and ‘U’ or ‘u’ (upper) that are often used as parameters to legacy BLAS implementations.

member.name: F:CUDA.cublasFillMode.CUBLAS_FILL_MODE_LOWER
member.summary: the lower part of the matrix is filled

member.name: F:CUDA.cublasFillMode.CUBLAS_FILL_MODE_UPPER
member.summary: the upper part of the matrix is filled

member.name: T:CUDA.cublasDiagType
member.summary: (cuBLAS) The type indicates whether the main diagonal of the dense matrix is unity and consequently should not be touched or modified by the function. Its values correspond to Fortran characters ‘N’ or ‘n’ (non-unit) and ‘U’ or ‘u’ (unit) that are often used as parameters to legacy BLAS implementations.

member.name: F:CUDA.cublasDiagType.CUBLAS_DIAG_NON_UNIT
member.summary: the matrix diagonal has non-unit elements

member.name: F:CUDA.cublasDiagType.CUBLAS_DIAG_UNIT
member.summary: the matrix diagonal has unit elements

member.name: T:CUDA.cublasSideMode
member.summary: (cuBLAS) The type indicates whether the dense matrix is on the left or right side in the matrix equation solved by a particular function. Its values correspond to Fortran characters ‘L’ or ‘l’ (left) and ‘R’ or ‘r’ (right) that are often used as parameters to legacy BLAS implementations.

member.name: F:CUDA.cublasSideMode.CUBLAS_SIDE_LEFT
member.summary: the matrix is on the left side in the equation

member.name: F:CUDA.cublasSideMode.CUBLAS_SIDE_RIGHT
member.summary: the matrix is on the right side in the equation

member.name: T:CUDA.cublasPointerMode
member.summary: (cuBLAS) The cublasPointerMode_t type indicates whether the scalar values are passed by reference on the host or device.
member.remarks: It is important to point out that if several scalar values are present in the function call, all of them must conform to the same single pointer mode. The pointer mode can be set and retrieved using cublasSetPointerMode() and cublasGetPointerMode() routines, respectively.

member.name: F:CUDA.cublasPointerMode.CUBLAS_POINTER_MODE_HOST
member.summary: the scalars are passed by reference on the host

member.name: F:CUDA.cublasPointerMode.CUBLAS_POINTER_MODE_DEVICE
member.summary: the scalars are passed by reference on the device

member.name: T:CUDA.cublasAtomicsMode
member.summary: (cuBLAS) The type indicates whether cuBLAS routines which has an alternate implementation using atomics can be used. The atomics mode can be set and queried using and routines, respectively.

member.name: F:CUDA.cublasAtomicsMode.CUBLAS_ATOMICS_NOT_ALLOWED
member.summary: the usage of atomics is not allowed

member.name: F:CUDA.cublasAtomicsMode.CUBLAS_ATOMICS_ALLOWED
member.summary: the usage of atomics is allowed

Profiling session will continue and CUPTI will notify it using this error code. User is advised to recompile the application code with nvcc version 9.0 or later. member.name: F:CUDA.CUptiResult.CUPTI_ERROR_OPENACC_UNDEFINED_ROUTINE

One possible reason is that OpenACC library is linked statically in the user application, which might not have the definition of all the OpenACC API routines needed for the OpenACC profiling, as compiler might ignore definitions for the functions not used in the application. This issue can be mitigated by linking the OpenACC library dynamically.

member.name: M:CUDA.cuRAND.API.curandGenerate(System.IntPtr,System.UInt32[],System.Int64)
member.summary: Generate 32-bit pseudo or quasirandom numbers.
member.remarks: Use generator to generate num 32-bit results into the device memory at outputPtr. The device memory must have been previously allocated and be large enough to hold all the results. Launches are done with the stream set using curandSetStream(), or the null stream if no stream has been set. Results are 32-bit values with every bit random.
member.param: Generator to use
Pointer to device memory to store CUDA-generated results, or Pointer to host memory to store CPU-generated results
Number of random 32-bit values to generate

ul.li: CURAND_STATUS_NOT_INITIALIZED if the generator was never created
CURAND_STATUS_PREEXISTING_FAILURE if there was an existing error from a previous kernel launch
CURAND_STATUS_LENGTH_NOT_MULTIPLE if the number of output samples is not a multiple of the quasirandom dimension
CURAND_STATUS_LAUNCH_FAILURE if the kernel launch failed for any reason
CURAND_STATUS_TYPE_ERROR if the generator is a 64 bit quasirandom generator. (use curandGenerateLongLong() with 64 bit quasirandom generators)
CURAND_STATUS_SUCCESS if the results were generated successfully

member.name: M:CUDA.cuRAND.API.curandGenerateLogNormal(System.IntPtr,System.Single[],System.Int64,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Generate log-normally distributed floats.
member.remarks: Use generator to generate n float results into the device memory at outputPtr. The device memory must have been previously allocated and be large enough to hold all the results. Launches are done with the stream set using curandSetStream(), or the null stream if no stream has been set. Results are 32-bit floating point values with log-normal distribution based on an associated normal distribution with mean mean and standard deviation stddev. Normally distributed results are generated from pseudorandom generators with a Box-Muller transform, and so require n to be even.Quasirandom generators use an inverse cumulative distribution function to preserve dimensionality. The normally distributed results are transformed into log-normal distribution. There may be slight numerical differences between results generated on the GPU with generators created with curandCreateGenerator() and results calculated on the CPU with generators created with curandCreateGeneratorHost(). These differences arise because of differences in results for transcendental functions. In addition, future versions of CURAND may use newer versions of the CUDA math library, so different versions of CURAND may give slightly different numerical values.
member.param: Generator to use
Pointer to device memory to store CUDA-generated results, or Pointer to host memory to store CPU-generated results
Number of floats to generate
Mean of associated normal distribution
Standard deviation of associated normal distribution

ul.li: CURAND_STATUS_NOT_INITIALIZED if the generator was never created
CURAND_STATUS_PREEXISTING_FAILURE if there was an existing error from a previous kernel launch
CURAND_STATUS_LAUNCH_FAILURE if the kernel launch failed for any reason
CURAND_STATUS_LENGTH_NOT_MULTIPLE if the number of output samples is not a multiple of the quasirandom dimension, or is not a multiple of two for pseudorandom generators
CURAND_STATUS_SUCCESS if the results were generated successfully

member.name: F:CUDA.CUstreamWaitValue_flags.CU_STREAM_WAIT_VALUE_GEQ
member.summary: Wait until (int32_t)(*addr - value) >= 0. Note this is a cyclic comparison which ignores wraparound. (Default behavior.)

member.name: F:CUDA.CUstreamWaitValue_flags.CU_STREAM_WAIT_VALUE_EQ
member.summary: Wait until *addr == value.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUstreamWaitValue_flags.CU_STREAM_WAIT_VALUE_FLUSH
member.summary: Follow the wait operation with a flush of outstanding remote writes. This means that, if a remote write operation is guaranteed to have reached the device before the wait can be satisfied, that write is guaranteed to be visible to downstream device work. The device is permitted to reorder remote writes internally. For example, this flag would be required if two remote writes arrive in a defined order, the wait is satisfied by the second write, and downstream work needs to observe the first write.

member.name: T:CUDA.CUstreamWriteValue_flags
member.summary: (Driver API) Flags for ::cuStreamWriteValue32.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUstreamWriteValue_flags.CU_STREAM_WRITE_VALUE_DEFAULT
member.summary: Default behavior

member.name: F:CUDA.CUstreamWriteValue_flags.CU_STREAM_WRITE_VALUE_NO_MEMORY_BARRIER
member.summary: Permits the write to be reordered with writes which were issued before it, as a performance optimization. Normally, ::cuStreamWriteValue32 will provide a memory fence before the write, which has similar semantics to __threadfence_system() but is scoped to the stream rather than a CUDA thread.

member.summary: The size in bytes of statically-allocated shared memory required by this function. This does not include dynamically-allocated shared memory requested by the user at runtime.

member.summary: The size in bytes of user-allocated constant memory required by this function.

member.summary: The size in bytes of local memory used by each thread of this function.

member.summary: The number of registers used by each thread of this function.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUfunction_attribute.CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_PTX_VERSION
member.summary: The PTX virtual architecture version for which the function was compiled. This value is the major PTX version * 10 + the minor PTX version, so a PTX version 1.3 function would return the value 13. Note that this may return the undefined value of 0 for cubins compiled prior to CUDA 3.0.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUfunction_attribute.CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_BINARY_VERSION
member.summary: The binary architecture version for which the function was compiled. This value is the major binary version * 10 + the minor binary version, so a binary version 1.3 function would return the value 13. Note that this will return a value of 10 for legacy cubins that do not have a properly-encoded binary architecture version.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUfunction_attribute.CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_CACHE_MODE_CA
member.summary: The attribute to indicate whether the function has been compiled with user specified option "-Xptxas --dlcm=ca" set .

member.name: T:CUDA.CUjit_option
member.summary: (Driver API) Online compiler and linker options.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUjit_option.CU_JIT_MAX_REGISTERS
member.summary: Max number of registers that a thread may use. Option type: unsigned int Applies to: compiler only

member.name: F:CUDA.CUjit_option.CU_JIT_THREADS_PER_BLOCK
member.summary: IN: Specifies minimum number of threads per block to target compilation for OUT: Returns the number of threads the compiler actually targeted. This restricts the resource utilization fo the compiler (e.g. max registers) such that a block with the given number of threads should be able to launch based on register limitations. Note, this option does not currently take into account any other resource limitations, such as shared memory utilization. Cannot be combined with ::CU_JIT_TARGET. Option type: unsigned int Applies to: compiler only

member.name: F:CUDA.CUjit_option.CU_JIT_WALL_TIME
member.summary: Overwrites the option value with the total wall clock time, in milliseconds, spent in the compiler and linker Option type: float Applies to: compiler and linker

member.name: F:CUDA.CUjit_option.CU_JIT_INFO_LOG_BUFFER
member.summary: Pointer to a buffer in which to print any log messages that are informational in nature (the buffer size is specified via option ::CU_JIT_INFO_LOG_BUFFER_SIZE_BYTES) Option type: char * Applies to: compiler and linker

member.name: F:CUDA.CUjit_option.CU_JIT_INFO_LOG_BUFFER_SIZE_BYTES
member.summary: IN: Log buffer size in bytes. Log messages will be capped at this size (including null terminator) OUT: Amount of log buffer filled with messages Option type: unsigned int Applies to: compiler and linker

member.name: F:CUDA.CUjit_option.CU_JIT_ERROR_LOG_BUFFER
member.summary: Pointer to a buffer in which to print any log messages that reflect errors (the buffer size is specified via option ::CU_JIT_ERROR_LOG_BUFFER_SIZE_BYTES) Option type: char * Applies to: compiler and linker

member.name: F:CUDA.CUjit_option.CU_JIT_ERROR_LOG_BUFFER_SIZE_BYTES
member.summary: IN: Log buffer size in bytes. Log messages will be capped at this size (including null terminator) OUT: Amount of log buffer filled with messages Option type: unsigned int Applies to: compiler and linker

member.name: F:CUDA.CUjit_option.CU_JIT_OPTIMIZATION_LEVEL
member.summary: Level of optimizations to apply to generated code (0 - 4), with 4 being the default and highest level of optimizations. Option type: unsigned int Applies to: compiler only

member.name: F:CUDA.CUjit_option.CU_JIT_TARGET_FROM_CUCONTEXT
member.summary: No option value required. Determines the target based on the current attached context (default) Option type: No option value needed Applies to: compiler and linker

member.name: F:CUDA.CUjit_option.CU_JIT_TARGET
member.summary: Target is chosen based on supplied ::CUjit_target. Cannot be combined with ::CU_JIT_THREADS_PER_BLOCK. Option type: unsigned int for enumerated type ::CUjit_target Applies to: compiler and linker

member.name: F:CUDA.CUjit_option.CU_JIT_FALLBACK_STRATEGY
member.summary: Specifies choice of fallback strategy if matching cubin is not found. Choice is based on supplied ::CUjit_fallback. This option cannot be used with cuLink* APIs as the linker requires exact matches. Option type: unsigned int for enumerated type ::CUjit_fallback Applies to: compiler only

member.name: F:CUDA.CUjit_option.CU_JIT_GENERATE_DEBUG_INFO
member.summary: Specifies whether to create debug information in output (-g) (0: false, default) Option type: int Applies to: compiler and linker

member.name: F:CUDA.CUjit_option.CU_JIT_LOG_VERBOSE
member.summary: Generate verbose log messages (0: false, default) Option type: int Applies to: compiler and linker

member.name: F:CUDA.CUjit_option.CU_JIT_GENERATE_LINE_INFO
member.summary: Generate line number information (-lineinfo) (0: false, default) Option type: int Applies to: compiler only

member.name: F:CUDA.CUjit_option.CU_JIT_CACHE_MODE
member.summary:
Specifies whether to enable caching explicitly (-dlcm)
Choice is based on supplied ::CUjit_cacheMode_enum.
Option type: unsigned int for enumerated type ::CUjit_cacheMode_enum
Applies to: compiler only

member.name: T:CUDA.CUresult
member.summary: (Driver API) Error codes.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_SUCCESS
member.summary: The API call returned with no errors. In the case of query calls, this can also mean that the operation being queried is complete (see ::cuEventQuery() and ::cuStreamQuery()).

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE
member.summary: This indicates that one or more of the parameters passed to the API call is not within an acceptable range of values.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
member.summary: The API call failed because it was unable to allocate enough memory to perform the requested operation.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED
member.summary: This indicates that the CUDA driver has not been initialized with ::cuInit() or that initialization has failed.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_DEINITIALIZED
member.summary: This indicates that the CUDA driver is in the process of shutting down.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_PROFILER_DISABLED
member.summary: This indicates profiler is not initialized for this run. This can happen when the application is running with external profiling tools like visual profiler.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_PROFILER_NOT_INITIALIZED
member.summary: \deprecated This error return is deprecated as of CUDA 5.0. It is no longer an error to attempt to enable/disable the profiling via ::cuProfilerStart or ::cuProfilerStop without initialization.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_PROFILER_ALREADY_STARTED
member.summary: \deprecated This error return is deprecated as of CUDA 5.0. It is no longer an error to call cuProfilerStart() when profiling is already enabled.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_PROFILER_ALREADY_STOPPED
member.summary: \deprecated This error return is deprecated as of CUDA 5.0. It is no longer an error to call cuProfilerStop() when profiling is already disabled.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_NO_DEVICE
member.summary: This indicates that no CUDA-capable devices were detected by the installed CUDA driver.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_DEVICE
member.summary: This indicates that the device ordinal supplied by the user does not correspond to a valid CUDA device.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_IMAGE
member.summary: This indicates that the device kernel image is invalid. This can also indicate an invalid CUDA module.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_CONTEXT
member.summary: This most frequently indicates that there is no context bound to the current thread. This can also be returned if the context passed to an API call is not a valid handle (such as a context that has had ::cuCtxDestroy() invoked on it). This can also be returned if a user mixes different API versions (i.e. 3010 context with 3020 API calls). See ::cuCtxGetApiVersion() for more details.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_CONTEXT_ALREADY_CURRENT
member.summary: This indicated that the context being supplied as a parameter to the API call was already the active context. \deprecated This error return is deprecated as of CUDA 3.2. It is no longer an error to attempt to push the active context via ::cuCtxPushCurrent().

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_MAP_FAILED
member.summary: This indicates that a map or register operation has failed.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_UNMAP_FAILED
member.summary: This indicates that an unmap or unregister operation has failed.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_ARRAY_IS_MAPPED
member.summary: This indicates that the specified array is currently mapped and thus cannot be destroyed.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_ALREADY_MAPPED
member.summary: This indicates that the resource is already mapped.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_NO_BINARY_FOR_GPU
member.summary: This indicates that there is no kernel image available that is suitable for the device. This can occur when a user specifies code generation options for a particular CUDA source file that do not include the corresponding device configuration.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_ALREADY_ACQUIRED
member.summary: This indicates that a resource has already been acquired.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_NOT_MAPPED
member.summary: This indicates that a resource is not mapped.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_NOT_MAPPED_AS_ARRAY
member.summary: This indicates that a mapped resource is not available for access as an array.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_NOT_MAPPED_AS_POINTER
member.summary: This indicates that a mapped resource is not available for access as a pointer.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_ECC_UNCORRECTABLE
member.summary: This indicates that an uncorrectable ECC error was detected during execution.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_LIMIT
member.summary: This indicates that the ::CUlimit passed to the API call is not supported by the active device.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_CONTEXT_ALREADY_IN_USE
member.summary: This indicates that the ::CUcontext passed to the API call can only be bound to a single CPU thread at a time but is already bound to a CPU thread.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_PEER_ACCESS_UNSUPPORTED
member.summary: This indicates that peer access is not supported across the given devices.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_PTX
member.summary: This indicates that a PTX JIT compilation failed.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_GRAPHICS_CONTEXT
member.summary: This indicates an error with OpenGL or DirectX context.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_NVLINK_UNCORRECTABLE
member.summary: This indicates that an uncorrectable NVLink error was detected during the execution.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_SOURCE
member.summary: This indicates that the device kernel source is invalid.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND
member.summary: This indicates that the file specified was not found.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_SHARED_OBJECT_SYMBOL_NOT_FOUND
member.summary: This indicates that a link to a shared object failed to resolve.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_SHARED_OBJECT_INIT_FAILED
member.summary: This indicates that initialization of a shared object failed.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_OPERATING_SYSTEM
member.summary: This indicates that an OS call failed.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE
member.summary: This indicates that a resource handle passed to the API call was not valid. Resource handles are opaque types like ::CUstream and ::CUevent.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_NOT_FOUND
member.summary: This indicates that a named symbol was not found. Examples of symbols are global/constant variable names, texture names, and surface names.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_NOT_READY
member.summary: This indicates that asynchronous operations issued previously have not completed yet. This result is not actually an error, but must be indicated differently than ::CUDA_SUCCESS (which indicates completion). Calls that may return this value include ::cuEventQuery() and ::cuStreamQuery().

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS
member.summary: While executing a kernel, the device encountered a load or store instruction on an invalid memory address. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_OUT_OF_RESOURCES
member.summary: This indicates that a launch did not occur because it did not have appropriate resources. This error usually indicates that the user has attempted to pass too many arguments to the device kernel, or the kernel launch specifies too many threads for the kernel's register count. Passing arguments of the wrong size (i.e. a 64-bit pointer when a 32-bit int is expected) is equivalent to passing too many arguments and can also result in this error.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT
member.summary: This indicates that the device kernel took too long to execute. This can only occur if timeouts are enabled - see the device attribute ::CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_KERNEL_EXEC_TIMEOUT for more information. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_INCOMPATIBLE_TEXTURING
member.summary: This error indicates a kernel launch that uses an incompatible texturing mode.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_PEER_ACCESS_ALREADY_ENABLED
member.summary: This error indicates that a call to ::cuCtxEnablePeerAccess() is trying to re-enable peer access to a context which has already had peer access to it enabled.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_PEER_ACCESS_NOT_ENABLED
member.summary: This error indicates that ::cuCtxDisablePeerAccess() is trying to disable peer access which has not been enabled yet via ::cuCtxEnablePeerAccess().

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_PRIMARY_CONTEXT_ACTIVE
member.summary: This error indicates that the primary context for the specified device has already been initialized.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_CONTEXT_IS_DESTROYED
member.summary: This error indicates that the context current to the calling thread has been destroyed using ::cuCtxDestroy, or is a primary context which has not yet been initialized.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_ASSERT
member.summary: A device-side assert triggered during kernel execution. The context cannot be used anymore, and must be destroyed. All existing device memory allocations from this context are invalid and must be reconstructed if the program is to continue using CUDA.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_TOO_MANY_PEERS
member.summary: This error indicates that the hardware resources required to enable peer access have been exhausted for one or more of the devices passed to ::cuCtxEnablePeerAccess().

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_HOST_MEMORY_ALREADY_REGISTERED
member.summary: This error indicates that the memory range passed to ::cuMemHostRegister() has already been registered.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_HOST_MEMORY_NOT_REGISTERED
member.summary: This error indicates that the pointer passed to ::cuMemHostUnregister() does not correspond to any currently registered memory region.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_HARDWARE_STACK_ERROR
member.summary: While executing a kernel, the device encountered a stack error. This can be due to stack corruption or exceeding the stack size limit. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION
member.summary: While executing a kernel, the device encountered an illegal instruction. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_MISALIGNED_ADDRESS
member.summary: While executing a kernel, the device encountered a load or store instruction on a memory address which is not aligned. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_ADDRESS_SPACE
member.summary: While executing a kernel, the device encountered an instruction which can only operate on memory locations in certain address spaces (global, shared, or local), but was supplied a memory address not belonging to an allowed address space. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_PC
member.summary: While executing a kernel, the device program counter wrapped its address space. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED
member.summary: An exception occurred on the device while executing a kernel. Common causes include dereferencing an invalid device pointer and accessing out of bounds shared memory. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED
member.summary: This error indicates that the attempted operation is not permitted.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED
member.summary: This error indicates that the attempted operation is not supported on the current system or device.

member.name: F:CUDA.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN
member.summary: This indicates that an unknown internal error has occurred.

member.name: M:CUDA.NVRTC.API.nvrtcGetLoweredName(System.IntPtr,System.String,System.Text.StringBuilder@)
member.summary: nvrtcGetLoweredName extracts the lowered (mangled) name for a __global__ function or function template instantiation, and updates *lowered_name to point to it. The memory containing the name is released when the NVRTC program is destroyed by nvrtcDestroyProgram. The identical name expression must have been previously provided to nvrtcAddNameExpression.
member.param: CUDA Runtime Compilation program.
constant expression denoting a __global__ function or function template instantiation.
initialized by the function to point to a C string containing the lowered (mangled) name corresponding to the provided name expression.
member.returns: NVRTC_SUCCESS, NVRTC_ERROR_NO_LOWERED_NAMES_BEFORE_COMPILATION, NVRTC_ERROR_NAME_EXPRESSION_NOT_VALID

member.summary: The size in bytes of user-allocated constant memory required by this function.

member.summary: The size in bytes of local memory used by each thread of this function.

member.summary: The number of registers used by each thread of this function.

member.summary: The binary architecture version for which the function was compiled. This value is the major binary version * 10 + the minor binary version, so a binary version 1.3 function would return the value 13.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaPointerAttributes.device
member.summary: The device against which the memory was allocated or registered. If the memory type is ::cudaMemoryTypeDevice then this identifies the device on which the memory referred physically resides. If the memory type is ::cudaMemoryTypeHost then this identifies the device which was current when the memory was allocated or registered (and if that device is deinitialized then this allocation will vanish with that device's state).

member.summary: This indicates profiler is not initialized for this run. This can happen when the application is running with external profiling tools like visual profiler.

member.summary: It is no longer an error to attempt to enable/disable the profiling via cudaProfilerStart or cudaProfilerStop without initialization.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorProfilerAlreadyStarted
member.summary: It is no longer an error to call cudaProfilerStart() when profiling is already enabled.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorProfilerAlreadyStopped
member.summary: It is no longer an error to call cudaProfilerStop() when profiling is already disabled.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorInvalidConfiguration
member.summary: This indicates that a kernel launch is requesting resources that can never be satisfied by the current device.
member.remarks: Requesting more shared memory per block than the device supports will trigger this error, as will requesting too many threads or blocks. See cudaDeviceProp for more device limitations.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorInvalidPitchValue
member.summary: This indicates that one or more of the pitch-related parameters passed to the API call is not within the acceptable range for pitch.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorInvalidSymbol
member.summary: This indicates that the symbol name/identifier passed to the API call is not a valid name or identifier.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorInvalidHostPointer
member.summary: This indicates that at least one host pointer passed to the API call is not a valid host pointer.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorInvalidDevicePointer
member.summary: This indicates that at least one device pointer passed to the API call is not a valid device pointer.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorInvalidTexture
member.summary: This indicates that the texture passed to the API call is not a valid texture.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorInvalidTextureBinding
member.summary: This indicates that the texture binding is not valid. This occurs if you call cudaGetTextureAlignmentOffset() with an unbound texture.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorInvalidChannelDescriptor
member.summary: This indicates that the channel descriptor passed to the API call is not valid.
member.remarks: This occurs if the format is not one of the formats specified by cudaChannelFormatKind, or if one of the dimensions is invalid.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorInvalidMemcpyDirection
member.summary: This indicates that the direction of the memcpy passed to the API call is not one of the types specified by cudaMemcpyKind.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorInvalidFilterSetting
member.summary: This indicates that a non-float texture was being accessed with linear filtering. This is not supported by CUDA.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorInvalidNormSetting
member.summary: This indicates that an attempt was made to read a non-float texture as a normalized float. This is not supported by CUDA.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorInsufficientDriver
member.summary: This indicates that the installed NVIDIA CUDA driver is older than the CUDA runtime library. This is not a supported configuration. Users should install an updated NVIDIA display driver to allow the application to run.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorInvalidSurface
member.summary: This indicates that the surface passed to the API call is not a valid surface.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorDuplicateVariableName
member.summary: This indicates that multiple global or constant variables (across separate CUDA source files in the application) share the same string name.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorDuplicateTextureName
member.summary: This indicates that multiple textures (across separate CUDA source files in the application) share the same string name.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorDuplicateSurfaceName
member.summary: This indicates that multiple surfaces (across separate CUDA source files in the application) share the same string name.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorDevicesUnavailable
member.summary: This indicates that all CUDA devices are busy or unavailable at the current time.
member.remarks: Devices are often busy/unavailable due to use of cudaComputeModeExclusive, cudaComputeModeProhibited or when long running CUDA kernels have filled up the GPU and are blocking new work from starting. They can also be unavailable due to memory constraints on a device that already has active CUDA work being performed.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorIncompatibleDriverContext
member.summary: This indicates that the current context is not compatible with this the CUDA Runtime.
member.remarks: This can only occur if you are using CUDA Runtime/Driver interoperability and have created an existing Driver context using the driver API. The Driver context may be incompatible either because the Driver context was created using an older version of the API, because the Runtime API call expects a primary driver context and the Driver context is not primary, or because the Driver context has been destroyed. Please see Interactions with the CUDA Driver API" for more information.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorMissingConfiguration
member.summary: The device function being invoked (usually via cudaLaunchKernel()) was not previously configured via the cudaConfigureCall() function.

members.member: [Obsolete("This error return is deprecated as of CUDA 3.1")]

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorLaunchMaxDepthExceeded
member.summary: This error indicates that a device runtime grid launch did not occur because the depth of the child grid would exceed the maximum supported number of nested grid launches.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorLaunchFileScopedTex
member.summary: This error indicates that a grid launch did not occur because the kernel uses file-scoped textures which are unsupported by the device runtime. Kernels launched via the device runtime only support textures created with the Texture Object API's.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorLaunchFileScopedSurf
member.summary: This error indicates that a grid launch did not occur because the kernel uses file-scoped surfaces which are unsupported by the device runtime. Kernels launched via the device runtime only support surfaces created with the Surface Object API's.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorSyncDepthExceeded
member.summary: This error indicates that a call to cudaDeviceSynchronize made from the device runtime failed because the call was made at grid depth greater than than either the default (2 levels of grids) or user specified device limit cudaLimitDevRuntimeSyncDepth.
member.remarks: To be able to synchronize on launched grids at a greater depth successfully, the maximum nested depth at which cudaDeviceSynchronize will be called must be specified with the cudaLimitDevRuntimeSyncDepth limit to the cudaDeviceSetLimit api before the host-side launch of a kernel using the device runtime. Keep in mind that additional levels of sync depth require the runtime to reserve large amounts of device memory that cannot be used for user allocations.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorLaunchPendingCountExceeded
member.summary: This error indicates that a device runtime grid launch failed because the launch would exceed the limit cudaLimitDevRuntimePendingLaunchCount.
member.remarks: For this launch to proceed successfully, cudaDeviceSetLimit must be called to set the cudaLimitDevRuntimePendingLaunchCount to be higher than the upper bound of outstanding launches that can be issued to the device runtime. Keep in mind that raising the limit of pending device runtime launches will require the runtime to reserve device memory that cannot be used for user allocations.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorInvalidDeviceFunction
member.summary: The requested device function does not exist or is not compiled for the proper device architecture.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorNoDevice
member.summary: This indicates that no CUDA-capable devices were detected by the installed CUDA driver.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorInvalidDevice
member.summary: This indicates that the device ordinal supplied by the user does not correspond to a valid CUDA device.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorStartupFailure
member.summary: This indicates an internal startup failure in the CUDA runtime.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorInvalidKernelImage
member.summary: This indicates that the device kernel image is invalid.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorDeviceUninitialized
member.summary: This most frequently indicates that there is no context bound to the current thread. This can also be returned if the context passed to an API call is not a valid handle (such as a context that has had cuCtxDestroy() invoked on it). This can also be returned if a user mixes different API versions (i.e. 3010 context with 3020 API calls). See cuCtxGetApiVersion() for more details.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorMapBufferObjectFailed
member.summary: This indicates that the buffer object could not be mapped.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorUnmapBufferObjectFailed
member.summary: This indicates that the buffer object could not be unmapped.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorArrayIsMapped

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorAlreadyMapped

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorNoKernelImageForDevice
member.summary: This indicates that there is no kernel image available that is suitable for the device. This can occur when a user specifies code generation options for a particular CUDA source file that do not include the corresponding device configuration.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorAlreadyAcquired
member.summary: This indicates that a resource has already been acquired.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorNotMapped
member.summary: This indicates that a resource is not mapped.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorNotMappedAsArray
member.summary: This indicates that a mapped resource is not available for access as an array.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorNotMappedAsPointer
member.summary: This indicates that a mapped resource is not available for access as a pointer.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorECCUncorrectable
member.summary: This indicates that an uncorrectable ECC error was detected during execution.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorUnsupportedLimit
member.summary: This indicates that the cudaLimit passed to the API call is not supported by the active device.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorDeviceAlreadyInUse
member.summary: This indicates that a call tried to access an exclusive-thread device that is already in use by a different thread.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorPeerAccessUnsupported
member.summary: This error indicates that P2P access is not supported across the given devices.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorInvalidPtx
member.summary: A PTX compilation failed. The runtime may fall back to compiling PTX if an application does not contain a suitable binary for the current device.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorInvalidGraphicsContext
member.summary: This indicates an error with the OpenGL or DirectX context.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorNvlinkUncorrectable
member.summary: This indicates that an uncorrectable NVLink error was detected during the execution.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorJitCompilerNotFound
member.summary: This indicates that the PTX JIT compiler library was not found. The JIT Compiler library is used for PTX compilation. The runtime may fall back to compiling PTX if an application does not contain a suitable binary for the current device.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorInvalidSource
member.summary: This indicates that the device kernel source is invalid.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorFileNotFound
member.summary: This indicates that the file specified was not found.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorSharedObjectSymbolNotFound
member.summary: This indicates that a link to a shared object failed to resolve.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorSharedObjectInitFailed
member.summary: This indicates that initialization of a shared object failed.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorOperatingSystem
member.summary: This error indicates that an OS call failed.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorInvalidResourceHandle
member.summary: This indicates that a resource handle passed to the API call was not valid. Resource handles are opaque types like cudaStream_t and cudaEvent_t.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorIllegalState
member.summary: This indicates that a resource required by the API call is not in a valid state to perform the requested operation.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorSymbolNotFound
member.summary: This indicates that a named symbol was not found. Examples of symbols are global/constant variable names, texture names, and surface names.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorNotReady
member.summary: This indicates that asynchronous operations issued previously have not completed yet. This result is not actually an error, but must be indicated differently than cudaSuccess (which indicates completion). Calls that may return this value include cudaEventQuery() and cudaStreamQuery().

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorIllegalAddress
member.summary: The device encountered a load or store instruction on an invalid memory address. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorLaunchOutOfResources
member.summary: This indicates that a launch did not occur because it did not have appropriate resources. Although this error is similar to cudaErrorInvalidConfiguration, this error usually indicates that the user has attempted to pass too many arguments to the device kernel, or the kernel launch specifies too many threads for the kernel's register count.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorLaunchTimeout
member.summary: This indicates that the device kernel took too long to execute. This can only occur if timeouts are enabled - see the device property kernelExecTimeoutEnabled for more information. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorLaunchIncompatibleTexturing
member.summary: This error indicates a kernel launch that uses an incompatible texturing mode.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorPeerAccessAlreadyEnabled
member.summary: This error indicates that a call to cudaDeviceEnablePeerAccess() is trying to re-enable peer addressing on from a context which has already had peer addressing enabled.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorPeerAccessNotEnabled
member.summary: This error indicates that cudaDeviceDisablePeerAccess() is trying to disable peer addressing which has not been enabled yet via cudaDeviceEnablePeerAccess().

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorSetOnActiveProcess
member.summary: This indicates that the user has called cudaSetValidDevices(), cudaSetDeviceFlags(), cudaD3D9SetDirect3DDevice(), cudaD3D10SetDirect3DDevice, cudaD3D11SetDirect3DDevice(), or cudaVDPAUSetVDPAUDevice() after initializing the CUDA runtime by calling non-device management operations (allocating memory and launching kernels are examples of non-device management operations). This error can also be returned if using runtime/driver interoperability and there is an existing CUcontext active on the host thread.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorContextIsDestroyed
member.summary: This error indicates that the context current to the calling thread has been destroyed using cuCtxDestroy, or is a primary context which has not yet been initialized.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorAssert
member.summary: An assert triggered in device code during kernel execution. The device cannot be used again. All existing allocations are invalid. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorTooManyPeers
member.summary: This error indicates that the hardware resources required to enable peer access have been exhausted for one or more of the devices passed to cudaEnablePeerAccess().

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorHostMemoryAlreadyRegistered
member.summary: This error indicates that the memory range passed to cudaHostRegister() has already been registered.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorHostMemoryNotRegistered
member.summary: This error indicates that the pointer passed to cudaHostUnregister() does not correspond to any currently registered memory region.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorHardwareStackError
member.summary: Device encountered an error in the call stack during kernel execution, possibly due to stack corruption or exceeding the stack size limit. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorIllegalInstruction
member.summary: The device encountered an illegal instruction during kernel execution This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorMisalignedAddress
member.summary: The device encountered a load or store instruction on a memory address which is not aligned. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorInvalidAddressSpace
member.summary: While executing a kernel, the device encountered an instruction which can only operate on memory locations in certain address spaces (global, shared, or local), but was supplied a memory address not belonging to an allowed address space. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorInvalidPc
member.summary: The device encountered an invalid program counter. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorLaunchFailure
member.summary: An exception occurred on the device while executing a kernel. Common causes include dereferencing an invalid device pointer and accessing out of bounds shared memory. Less common cases can be system specific - more information about these cases can be found in the system specific user guide. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorCooperativeLaunchTooLarge
member.summary: This error indicates that the number of blocks launched per grid for a kernel that was launched via either cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel or cudaLaunchCooperativeKernelMultiDevice exceeds the maximum number of blocks as allowed by cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor or cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessorWithFlags times the number of multiprocessors as specified by the device attribute cudaDevAttrMultiProcessorCount.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorNotPermitted
member.summary: This error indicates the attempted operation is not permitted.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorNotSupported
member.summary: This error indicates the attempted operation is not supported on the current system or device.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorSystemNotReady
member.summary: This error indicates that the system is not yet ready to start any CUDA work. To continue using CUDA, verify the system configuration is in a valid state and all required driver daemons are actively running. More information about this error can be found in the system specific user guide.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorSystemDriverMismatch
member.summary: This error indicates that there is a mismatch between the versions of the display driver and the CUDA driver. Refer to the compatibility documentation for supported versions.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorCompatNotSupportedOnDevice
member.summary: This error indicates that the system was upgraded to run with forward compatibility but the visible hardware detected by CUDA does not support this configuration. Refer to the compatibility documentation for the supported hardware matrix or ensure that only supported hardware is visible during initialization via the CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES environment variable.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorStreamCaptureUnsupported
member.summary: The operation is not permitted when the stream is capturing.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorStreamCaptureInvalidated
member.summary: The current capture sequence on the stream has been invalidated due to a previous error.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorStreamCaptureMerge
member.summary: The operation would have resulted in a merge of two independent capture sequences.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorStreamCaptureUnmatched
member.summary: The capture was not initiated in this stream.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorStreamCaptureUnjoined
member.summary: The capture sequence contains a fork that was not joined to the primary stream.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorStreamCaptureIsolation
member.summary: A dependency would have been created which crosses the capture sequence boundary. Only implicit in-stream ordering dependencies are allowed to cross the boundary.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorStreamCaptureImplicit
member.summary: The operation would have resulted in a disallowed implicit dependency on a current capture sequence from cudaStreamLegacy.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorCapturedEvent
member.summary: The operation is not permitted on an event which was last recorded in a capturing stream.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorStreamCaptureWrongThread
member.summary: A stream capture sequence not initiated with the cudaStreamCaptureModeRelaxed argument to cudaStreamBeginCapture was passed to cudaStreamEndCapture in a different thread.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorTimeout
member.summary: This indicates that the wait operation has timed out.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorGraphExecUpdateFailure
member.summary: This error indicates that the graph update was not performed because it included changes which violated constraints specific to instantiated graph update.

member.name: F:CUDA.cudaError.cudaErrorUnknown
